question: Should implementation begin on the bounded recovery that restores a trustworthy Claude, Codex, and Pi live signal before one CI confirmation?
summary: Approve implementation. Independent staff review confirms that all nine current failures are classified from retained evidence: five impossible-state gate failures and Codex keep-moving are stale oracles; Claude Opus recorded lifecycle is a cwd-sensitive harness extraction defect; Codex rejection flow is a lifecycle-invalid fixture; and Pi recorded lifecycle is a real conduct defect because its review never reaches the root assistant channel. The repair preserves every approved journey and changes 12 existing files, estimated at +167/-49 handwritten lines with no generated or golden churn. It must stop for re-approval above 14 files or 292 changed lines. The Pi correction changes only semantic channel and ordering, never prescribed wording, commands, recommendations, or decisions. Focused host tests run first; then the complete local Sonnet, Opus, Codex, and Pi suites must all pass from the same tip before a single full CI run. No scenario withdrawal, prompt coaching, quarantine, compatibility layer, new standing harness, or CI-led iteration is allowed. Staff review completed three correction cycles and recommends approval with no material, deferred, or polish findings. A final deterministic gate check corrected the criteria to canonical AC-1 through AC-5 identifiers and explicitly re-anchors the four mechanism criteria to the 4/4 same-tip value criterion.

artifacts.summary: Canonical design, nine-failure classification, acceptance criteria AC-1 through AC-5, exact 12-file surface, local proof commands, and ideation reports through cycle 4.

routes.label: Keep the release blocker at ideation
